terms.grammar: in an address, the ablative after the street: in viā Aureliā, numerō sextō
evidence: Levi–Bini p. 267: In viā Aureliā, numerō VI, tabulātō secundō
terms.comment: Classically a number of any kind; the numbering of houses is modern, and so is this use, which follows Levi–Bini’s addresses (street, number, and floor, each in the ablative). A Roman gave his address by landmarks instead, as Martial does: by the Pear Tree, up three flights, opposite Caesar’s forum.

phrases.latin: Ubi habitās? — In viā Aureliā, numerō VI, tabulātō secundō.
phrases.english: Where do you live? — In Via Aurelia, number 6, second floor.
What number does Grandma live at? — Seven.

phrases.latin: Argī nempe solēs subīre Lētum: contrā Caesaris est forum taberna
phrases.english: you often go down the Argiletum, of course: opposite Caesar’s forum there’s a shop

sources: Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 267, 293, s.v. via.
